unit.title: Precios, gustos y planes
unit.subtitle: How much is it?, like + -ing y cómo invitar

theory.title: How much is it? y los plurales con are
theory.body:
Para preguntar el precio: **How much is it?** (una cosa) · **How much are they?** (varias). También: *How much **does** it cost?*

Se responde con el mismo verbo: *It's twelve dollars.* · *They're twenty dollars.*

*$12.50* se dice **twelve fifty** o **twelve dollars and fifty cents**. En pesos: *fifty thousand pesos* (50.000); **thousand** no lleva -s después de un número. Y para opinar: *That's **expensive**.* · *That's **cheap**.*

Los plurales llevan **are**: *These shoes **are** cheap.* Ojo con los irregulares: **person → people** · **child → children** · **man → men** · **woman → women**. *People* ya es plural: ❌ *the peoples* (*peoples* solo existe como «pueblos, naciones»).
theory.trap: De «¿cuánto cuesta?» sale *How much cost?*, pero al inglés le falta el sujeto y el ayudante: **How much is it?** o **How much does it cost?** Y como «los zapatos» ya suena a varios, se escapa el verbo: ❌ *the shoes is* → ✅ **the shoes are**. Tampoco *the peoples*: **people** ya es plural.

exercises.tip: shoes es plural, así que va are. Y el precio se pregunta con much, no con many.

accept: How much does this shirt cost?
What does this shirt cost?
exercises.tip: «¿Cuánto cuesta?» = How much is...? Si preguntas con el verbo cost, hace falta does: How much does it cost?

exercises.text: It's twelve dollars and fifty cents.
exercises.tip: Cierra bien las finales: dollars con z, cents con ts. Si las sueltas, suena «dolar» y «cen».
These (estos) y are van con plural: these shoes are.
Escucha bien el número: twenty (20) y twelve (12) empiezan igual.

accept: It's expensive.
That's pricey.
exercises.tip: Hace falta el sujeto: that's (o it's). Y sin a delante del adjetivo solo.

accept: It's 50,000 pesos.
exercises.tip: thousand = mil, y no lleva -s después de un número: fifty thousand, no fifty thousands.

exercises.text: How much ___ they?
exercises.tip: they es plural: are.

exercises.text: She wants cheap shoes.
exercises.tip: She y shoes empiezan con sh suave, como cuando pides silencio. cheap sí es ch, con la t pegada: no las confundas.

exercises.es: Hay muchas personas en la tienda.
exercises.answer: There are a lot of people in the store.
accept: There are many people in the store.
There are lots of people in the store.
There are a lot of people at the store.
There are many people at the store.
There are lots of people at the store.
There are a lot of people in the shop.
There are many people in the shop.
There are lots of people in the shop.
There are a lot of people at the shop.
There are many people at the shop.
There are lots of people at the shop.
exercises.tip: people ya es plural (personas): va con are y nunca lleva -s.
fifteen (15) carga la fuerza al final y alarga la i: fif-TEEN. fifty (50) la carga al principio: FIF-ty.

exercises.es: Los niños están en el parque.
exercises.text: The ___ are in the park.
accept: kids
boys
exercises.tip: child → children. Plural irregular: no se dice childs.

accept: It's twelve dollars and fifty cents.
It costs twelve fifty.
It costs twelve dollars and fifty cents.
It's twelve dollars fifty.
It costs twelve dollars fifty.
It costs $12.50.
exercises.tip: Con precios se usa it's o it costs. «Doce con cincuenta» se dice twelve fifty.

exercises.text: How much is it? It's twelve fifty.
exercises.tip: twelve fifty sale de corrido, como un solo número.

theory.title: like + -ing: el que gusta eres tú
theory.body:
En inglés la persona va primero y el verbo es **like**: *I like coffee.* (Me gusta el café.)

Después de **like, love, hate, enjoy** y **don't mind** (no me molesta) va una cosa o un verbo con **-ing**:
*I **like cooking**.* · *She **loves dancing**.* · *I **don't mind** waiting.*

Con like, love y hate también se oye **to**: *I like to cook.* Con enjoy y don't mind, solo -ing.

Preguntar: ***Do you like** soccer? — Yes, I **do**. / No, I **don't**.*

Y no confundas: **I like** = me gusta (en general). **I'd like** = quisiera (ahora).
theory.trap: «Me gusta» está al revés: no es *It likes me* sino **I like it**. Y lo que sigue va directo: ❌ *I like to the music* · ❌ *I love cook* → ✅ **I like music** · **I love cooking**. El «mucho» va al final: ❌ *I like very much soccer* → ✅ **I like soccer very much**.

exercises.tip: Después de like, el verbo va con -ing (cooking) o con to (to cook), pero no los dos.

accept: I love to swim.
exercises.tip: love + -ing. swim dobla la m: swimming.

exercises.text: She hates washing the dishes.
exercises.tip: sh en she, washing y dishes: suave y largo, sin la t de ch.
don't mind = no me molesta. Después va el verbo con -ing.

accept: Do you like to dance?
Do you enjoy dancing?
exercises.tip: Do you like...? pregunta por tus gustos. Would you like to dance? es una invitación: ¿quieres bailar (ahora)?

exercises.audio: Yes, I do. I love it.
options: Yes, I like. I love it.
Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.answer: Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta repite el ayudante: Yes, I do. Y love necesita su objeto: I love it.

exercises.es: Me gusta leer por la noche.
exercises.text: I like ___ at night.
accept: to read
exercises.tip: like + -ing: reading. También vale to read.

exercises.meaning: A mi hermano no le gusta ir de compras.
exercises.tip: doesn't se lleva la -s: like queda sin -s. shopping dobla la p.

exercises.text: He hates his job.
exercises.tip: Las tres h suenan: un soplo suave, como cuando empañas un vidrio. No es la j española.

accept: I like soccer very much.
I really like soccer.
I like soccer so much.
I like football a lot.
I like football very much.
I really like football.
I like football so much.
exercises.tip: El «mucho» va al final: I like soccer a lot. En Estados Unidos el fútbol es soccer.

exercises.text: Do you like cooking? — Yes, I ___.
exercises.tip: La respuesta corta usa el ayudante de la pregunta: Do you...? → Yes, I do.

exercises.es: A ella le gusta caminar, pero odia correr.
exercises.answer: She likes walking, but she hates running.
accept: She likes walking but hates running.
She likes to walk, but she hates to run.
She likes to walk but hates to run.
She likes to walk, but she hates running.
She likes to walk but hates running.
She likes walking, but she hates to run.
She likes walking but hates to run.
exercises.tip: Con she, los dos verbos llevan -s: likes, hates. running dobla la n.

exercises.text: Do you like dancing? Yes, I do. I love it.
exercises.tip: Pregunta subiendo al final; la respuesta, bajando.

theory.title: Proponer e invitar
theory.body:
Para proponer algo entre todos: **Let's** + verbo, sin to.
*Let's go to the movies.* · *Let's not wait.*

Para invitar: **Would you like to** + verbo (la más amable) o **Do you want to** + verbo.
*Would you like to come?* · *Do you want to eat something?*

**How about** + una cosa: *How about pizza?* · *How about Friday?* O un verbo con **-ing**, como después de like: *How about going out?*

Aceptar: *Sure!* · *I'd love to.* · *Sounds good.*
Rechazar con cortesía: *Sorry, I can't. I'm busy.*
theory.trap: «Vamos a...» empuja a poner to: ❌ *Let's to go*. Después de **let's** el verbo va pelado: **Let's go**. Con would like pasa lo contrario, sí lleva to: ❌ *Would you like come?* → ✅ **Would you like to come?** Y «¿quieres que vaya?» no se arma con that: ❌ *Do you want that I go?* → ✅ **Do you want me to go?**

options: Let's to go to the movies.
exercises.tip: Let's + verbo pelado: let's go. Ir al cine = go to the movies.

options: Would you like come to my house?
Would you like to come to my house?
Do you like to come to my house?
exercises.answer: Would you like to come to my house?
accept: Do you want to come to my house?
Would you like to come over?
Do you want to come over?
Would you like to come to my place?
Would you like to come over to my house?
Do you want to come over to my house?
Do you want to come to my place?
exercises.tip: Would you like + to + verbo. Do you like...? pregunta por gustos, no invita.

exercises.text: Sure! I'd love to.
exercises.tip: La v de love se hace con los dientes de arriba sobre el labio de abajo. No la cambies por b.

accept: Today, let's not go.
exercises.tip: Para negar una propuesta: let's not + verbo.

exercises.es: Lo siento, no puedo. Estoy ocupado.
options: Sorry, I don't can. I'm busy.
Sorry, I can't. I have busy.
accept: I'm sorry, I can't. I'm busy.
Sorry, I can't make it. I'm busy.
I'm sorry, I can't make it. I'm busy.
exercises.tip: Ocupado es un estado: I'm busy (con be), no I have busy.

exercises.text: Do you want ___ eat something?
exercises.tip: want pide to antes del verbo: want to eat.
How about + una cosa o un día, sin to: How about Friday night?

exercises.audio: Sounds good. See you at eight.
accept: Sounds good. See you at 8:00.
exercises.meaning: Me parece bien. Nos vemos a las ocho.
exercises.tip: Sounds good = me parece bien. Es una forma corta de aceptar.

exercises.text: How about this Thursday?
exercises.tip: this y Thursday llevan th: la punta de la lengua asoma entre los dientes. En this vibra; en Thursday es solo aire.

accept: Let's have pizza tonight.
Let's get pizza tonight.
Let's eat some pizza tonight.
Let's have some pizza tonight.
Let's get some pizza tonight.
Tonight let's eat pizza.
Let's eat pizza this evening.
Let's have pizza this evening.
Tonight let's have pizza.
Tonight let's get pizza.
exercises.tip: «Comamos» es una propuesta: let's + verbo.

exercises.text: Would you like to dance? — I'd ___ to!
exercises.tip: I'd love to = me encantaría. El to del final reemplaza al verbo: no hace falta repetir dance.

exercises.answer: Do you want to come with us?
accept: Would you like to come with us?
Want to come with us?
Do you want to join us?
Would you like to join us?
Do you want to go with us?
Would you like to go with us?
Do you want to come along with us?
Would you like to come along with us?
exercises.tip: Do you want + to + verbo. Con would you like suena más amable.

exercises.text: Let's go to the movies. Sure, sounds good!
exercises.tip: Let's go sale como una sola palabra: «letsgou».

unit.title: Preguntar por el pasado
unit.subtitle: Where did you go?, había y respuestas cortas

theory.title: Where did you go? y «había»
theory.body:
Para preguntar en pasado con **where, what, when, who**: palabra de pregunta + **did** + sujeto + verbo **normal**.
*Where **did** you **go**?* · *When **did** she **arrive**?* (Si **who** es quien hizo la acción, va sin did: *Who called?*)

Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I **did**.* · *No, he **didn't**.* Con be: *Yes, it **was**.*

**Había** (cuando significa «existía») es el pasado de *there is / there are*:
**there was** + una cosa (o algo que no se cuenta: *a lot of noise*) · **there were** + varias
*There **was** a party.* · *There **were** many people.*
Pregunta: ***Was there** a problem?* · ***Were there** many people?*
theory.trap: En español basta la entonación, y sale *Where you went?*; o, mezclando, *Where did you went?* Con **did** el verbo vuelve a su forma normal: **Where did you go?** Y el «había» de existir no es *had* ni *there had*: ❌ *Had a party* → ✅ **There was a party**. Con gente va were: ❌ *There was many people* → ✅ **There were many people**.

exercises.tip: El pasado ya está en did: el verbo queda en go, no en went.

options: What you did on the weekend?
What did you do on the weekend?
What did you did on the weekend?
exercises.answer: What did you do on the weekend?
accept: What did you do over the weekend?
What did you do this weekend?
What did you do last weekend?
What did you do this past weekend?
What did you do at the weekend?
exercises.tip: What + did + you + do: el primer do es el ayudante (did), el segundo es el verbo hacer.

exercises.text: There were a lot of people there.
exercises.tip: There lleva th que vibra: lengua entre los dientes, no una d.
Con did, arrive sin -ed. Y llegó es pasado: did, no does.
people es plural: there were. «Había» nunca se dice con had.

accept: Was there an issue?
Was there any problem?
exercises.tip: Para preguntar se voltea: there was → was there?

exercises.text: Who ___ you see at the party?
exercises.tip: Aquí who es a quien viste (tú viste): hace falta did y see queda normal.

exercises.audio: No, she didn't. She stayed home.
exercises.meaning: No, ella no. Se quedó en casa.
exercises.tip: Respuesta corta: No, she didn't, sin repetir el verbo.

exercises.text: What did you do last weekend?
exercises.tip: Cierra las finales: la d de did, la st de last, la d de weekend.
Where + did + you + go. Nada de went después de did.

exercises.text: Was the movie good? — Yes, it ___.
exercises.tip: Si la pregunta va con was, la respuesta corta también: Yes, it was.

exercises.answer: Were there a lot of people at the concert?
accept: Were there many people at the concert?
Were there lots of people at the concert?
Was the concert crowded?
Was it crowded at the concert?
Was there a big crowd at the concert?
exercises.tip: gente = people, que es plural: were there, no was there.

exercises.text: Where did you go? Was there a party?
exercises.tip: La pregunta con where baja al final; la de sí o no (Was there...?) sube.
